chunks: He said: Abu Hafs Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi reported to me, saying: Abu al-Husayn al-Abbas ibn al-Mughirah al-Jawhari narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Anbasah narrated to us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said:

When death was approaching the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, and in the house were men, among them Umar ibn al-Khattab, the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family and grant him peace, said: "Come, let me write for you a document after which you will never go astray!" So Umar said: "Do not bring him anything, for indeed the pain has overwhelmed him, and you have the Quran — the Book of Allah is sufficient for us." Then the people in the house differed and disputed among themselves. Some of them said: "Rise, let the Messenger of Allah write for you," while others said what Umar had said. When the commotion and dispute increased, the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family and grant him peace, said: "Go away from me."

Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah said: And Ibn Abbas, may Allah have mercy on him, used to say: "The calamity — the total calamity — was what stood between the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, and his writing that document for us, because of their dispute and commotion."

key_terms.الرزية: calamity, catastrophe — used by Ibn Abbas to describe this event as the greatest tragedy for the Muslim community
key_terms.اللغط: commotion, noisy dispute — refers to the disorderly uproar that prevented the Prophet from writing
key_terms.حسبنا كتاب الله: the Book of Allah is sufficient for us — Umar's response rejecting the need for additional written guidance
key_terms.كتاباً لن تضلوا بعده أبداً: a document after which you will never go astray — the Prophet's promise of a definitive written testament

ai.seo_question: What happened when Prophet Muhammad asked for pen and paper on his deathbed?
ai.summary: This is the famous 'Calamity of Thursday' (Raziyyat al-Khamis), one of the most significant events in Islamic history. As the Prophet Muhammad lay on his deathbed, he requested writing materials to compose a testament that would prevent the ummah from ever going astray. Umar ibn al-Khattab objected, claiming the Prophet was overwhelmed by pain and that the Quran was sufficient. The ensuing dispute among those present caused the Prophet to dismiss them in sorrow. Ibn Abbas, who witnessed this as a young man, lamented this as the greatest calamity that befell the Muslim community, as it prevented the Prophet from documenting his final guidance — which Shia scholars understand as his intended designation of Ali ibn Abi Talib as successor.
